title: SoC/HotWax
summary:
The meeting covered fulfillment-system improvements, replenishment behavior, shipping-label integrations, and holiday order-planning requirements. Discussions focused on resolving operational issues while preparing integrations and workflows for peak-season testing.

A packing-label fix for box changes during packing was included in the latest release. The issue appeared related to parallel transactions and possible deadlocks rather than carrier behavior. The team also refined picker-performance reporting requirements, including picker identity, product category, location or area, and picking duration. Looker access may need to be restored for dashboard configuration.

The team reviewed alternatives for removing the additional “start picking” interaction under ticket SOC 1039. Replenishment drop-off logic will initially provide flexible suggestions based on inventory conditions and location availability. Soup locations may accept any soup flavor when inventory is zero rather than reserving specific locations for fixed SKUs. More restrictive SKU-to-location assignments remain possible through the existing data model. Replenishment changes are expected to be evaluated and deployed during the planned PA visit, scheduled for September 14–October 2 or potentially September 21–October 9.

A refactored inventory configuration screen clarifies product, facility, and location associations and was ready for review in UAT. The Jitsu integration requires development work covering credentials, shipment creation, and label generation. Its proposed September 9 delivery may conflict with the requirement to be operational by September 11, begin test shipments September 14, and allow one week of testing beforehand.

The shipping-label integration is expected to use a PDF format consistent with the B-home configuration, although production details remain under review. The team examined Jitsu shipment and label JSON schemas and demonstrated converting a returned ZPL label into a printable format. SAPI endpoints and other production requirements remain outstanding.

When a replenishment source location is locked, users receive a notification, affected tasks are canceled, and the next scheduled job searches unlocked inventory locations. Automatically canceled tasks now include a system comment identifying the locked source. The production behavior of the required reason for “Skip item” remains unresolved. Order-routing test JSONs and import instructions were also pending, as was investigation of a product showing zero online inventory or ATP.

Holiday order planning primarily requires filtering by ship-by date, ship-after date, and days in transit rather than displaying every underlying order field. Transit duration is derived from carrier postal-route mapping after routing and can vary by destination despite the same ground service. The intended process uses manual pick waivers followed by payment creation, without changing peak profiles.

The complete workflow is expected to be tested in UAT using approximately 50–100 representative orders, including import, filtering, and pick-waiving scenarios. The process has not yet been validated with production-like orders, and expected behavior and recurring operational issues remain areas for review.
